post.description: Starts the instance on its worker (fire-and-forget: responds immediately). Requires the `instance:execute` permission. Quota checking and setting status to `starting` happen in one transaction; `starting` counts toward memory/CPU quotas until the worker reports running, stopped or failed. Duplicate start/restart requests while starting or a backup in progress return 400; the previous status is restored if the worker rejects the start. Checks the owner's disk, memory and CPU quotas before sending the command and returns 403 if a quota is exceeded. Worker communication failures return 503 before the response starts. A timeout does not confirm failure of the operation: check its resulting state before retrying. No automatic retry is performed. WORKER_TIMEOUT (default 300000 ms) covers the request and JSON response consumption. Unused control-command response bodies are cancelled; this deadline does not limit asynchronous game operations.
